title: Quarterly plan: capacity credit windows & adaptive prewarm strategy for Dedicated pools
creator: Aisha Martinez
description: Quarterly roadmap item to design and deliver a capacity credit windowing mechanism combined with an adaptive prewarm strategy for Dedicated pools. The goal is to reduce cold-start latency and lower effective unit cost by enabling flexible short-term reservation windows, improved tenant fairshare during surges, and workload-aware prewarm policies that respect SLA tiers. This ticket captures scope, milestones, success metrics, risks, and cross-team dependencies required for a Q2 pilot and Q3 rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Definition and spec for capacity credit windows published in Confluence with clear UI/CLI knobs
Adaptive prewarm algorithm implemented in runtime (canary) with telemetry proving 25% reduction in cold-start tail latency for target workloads
Billing model for short-window reservations defined and approved by finance
Canary execution on two dedicated pools with controlled traffic and rollback gates
Runbook and operator dashboard widgets added to Console for monitoring prewarm health and credit utilization

decisions: Use time-boxed credit windows (default 1 hour, configurable 15m-6h) rather than per-minute billing to limit accounting complexity
Prewarm policy will be hierarchical: SLA tier override -> tenant budget cap -> workload-signature heuristic
Canary will limit prewarm to 5% of pool size in initial test to avoid large cost exposure
risks: Over-prewarm could blow quarterly compute budget if heuristics are too permissive
Fairshare implementation could introduce latency variance for low-priority tenants
Billing edge-cases for overlapping windows require careful accounting to avoid double-billing
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Lab experiments with historical traces to validate heuristics
Phase 1: Runtime prototype in isolated canary pool with synthetic traffic
Phase 2: Customer pilot with 3 willing customers (opt-in) and monitoring SLA regressions
Phase 3: Gradual ramp across regions with quota and budget guardrails
metrics: Cold-start P95 latency for dedicated pools (baseline vs pilot)
Prewarm utilization rate (tokens served by prewarmed instances)
Cost delta per million tokens for customers in pilot
Number of fallback events where prewarm failed and fallback model used
notes: Alternative considered: pure predictive warm pools based on demand forecasting — rejected for pilot due to complexity and data freshness requirements.
We will coordinate with Growth to recruit pilot customers; priority customers are those with predictable diurnal patterns.
Follow-up: evaluate combining credit windows with fractional pool shares as a next phase if pilot shows strong ROI.
